title: Chapter 127: Equipment Upgrade
html:
When the taxi stopped at the park entrance, Chen Ge called Xu Wan to help carry the boxes into the Haunted House.

“Boss, what’s inside these? They are so heavy.”

“Mannequin heads.” Chen Ge did not explain further. “Don’t open them if you’re easily scared.”

“Understood.”

Once the boxes were inside, Chen Ge sent Xu Wan to the dressing room to prepare while he sold tickets at the entrance.

With Mu Yang High School opening tomorrow, I need more staff. If necessary, I can ask Director Luo to lend me a park employee to sell tickets.

A man of about thirty interrupted his thoughts. “Mr. Chen? I finally found you.”

Few people addressed Chen Ge so formally. The stranger wore a casual suit and carried a black briefcase. His short hair was neatly styled, his smile broad, and his teeth dazzlingly white. “You were looking for me?”

“I haven’t missed a single livestream. They’re excellent.” The man opened with praise, but Chen Ge knew his own work. The content was unique, yet his poor equipment left plenty of room for improvement.

“You’re too kind.” Chen Ge still had no idea what the man was there for. “You’re a viewer?”

“I’m a devoted fan. I’ve followed you since your first video reached the midnight trending list. When Qin Guang copied your work, I posted your original on the forum and exposed his plagiarism.” Despite claiming devotion, the man remained perfectly composed, his smile polished and professional. He seemed to be entering a negotiation, not meeting an idol.

“Thank you.” Chen Ge did not entirely believe him, but the man appeared friendly and at least knew right from wrong. “Since you’re a fan, I’ll give you half off admission.”

“I don’t want to interrupt your business. Let the visitors behind me go first.” He stepped aside. Once Chen Ge had admitted the group and caught his breath, the man continued. “I heard Qin Guang’s studio sent people to cause trouble, but you taught them a lesson?”

“Those are only rumors. Qin Guang’s people have no scruples. They deliberately sent two psychiatric patients, then pretended to be victims when the pair had episodes inside my Haunted House. They tried to ruin my reputation. Shameless!” Chen Ge spoke through theatrically gritted teeth.

The man’s expression shifted before his smile returned. “I agree they were trying to frame you. Why would an ordinary visit to a Haunted House send them to the hospital? They should have invented a more believable excuse.”

“They ended up in the hospital?”

“Yes. They also threatened to cut off all your recommendation channels, but another studio stopped them.” The man grinned like a fox revealing its tail. “The platform belongs to everyone, not only Qin Guang.”

By then, Chen Ge understood. The man represented the rival studio. They must have a history with Qin Guang; otherwise, they would not have defended Chen Ge after discovering the plagiarism.

The viewership and recommendation channels for a platform were limited. If Qin Guang dominated all of them, it would cause a slow decline for the other creators.

“You came to propose a partnership, didn’t you? What should I call you?” Chen Ge eyed the briefcase and imagined it stuffed with cash.

“Actually, I’m also a host. You can call me Liu Dao.”

“Liu Dao?” Chen Ge nodded. “Then, what kind collaboration do you propose?”

“Supernatural livestreams have become unexpectedly popular, and naturally we want a share of that audience. Unfortunately, our studio lacks the right host. Even if we devoted every resource to one candidate, they still couldn’t surpass Qin Guang. His ethics leave much to be desired, but his streams are entertaining and he is charismatic.”

“So, you came to find me? I don’t think a normal guy like myself has more charisma than Qin Guang.”

“That’s where you’re wrong. I’ve watched your work, and whether you realize it or not, your streams are different.” Liu Dao’s smile vanished. “Viewers can usually spot a fake at a glance, including Qin Guang’s. He calls them supernatural livestreams, but they’re only a host inventing stories.

“However, yours is different.

“Your streams sustain an atmosphere of dread, as if mortal danger waits around every corner. Viewers experience the fear alongside you. That alone is remarkable.”

That’s because it is real!Even if Chen Ge confessed, Liu Dao would never believe him. “Perhaps I’m simply a good actor.”

“You’re too modest. Even professional actors can’t imitate that feeling of dancing on the edge of death.” Liu Dao’s admiration seemed genuine. “Your stream may be the only one capable of challenging Qin Guang. Work with us, and we’ll fight for every resource we can give you.”

“And what would you expect from me?” Chen Ge knew every reward came with a price.

“We’ll locate abandoned places, dress the sets, and prepare the scares. You only need to stream there and promote our studio in your channel.” Afraid Chen Ge might refuse, Liu Dao took a file from the briefcase. “We’ll provide the sets and scripts. One supernatural stream every ten days, scheduled against Qin Guang’s. Here are the proposed locations and outlines.”

These choices are far too safe. Some sets are beside residential areas; one careless camera movement would expose everything.

“You don’t think they’re suitable? I promise they’re completely safe. We’ll inspect every location beforehand and assign a camera operator to follow you during the stream.”

“You expect these to beat Qin Guang?” Chen Ge sighed and returned the file. “The locations are dull and the scripts predictable. Let me suggest somewhere instead.”

“What is it?”

“Have you heard of the Third Sick Hall?” Chen Ge turned on his phone and entered the name. Soon, many creepy, cruel, and insane headlines appeared on screen. “I plan to go here for my next livestream.”

Liu Dao scanned the articles. The uncensored photographs made his Adam’s apple bob. Wiping sweat from his forehead, he asked, “Are you sure? Isn’t this going too far?”
